subject: Refernce Genome not in Ensembl plus tiling windows analysis

messages.author: 8997e7809d3d7658
messages.subject: Refernce Genome not in Ensembl plus tiling windows analysis
parts:
Hi,

I have read the manuals and most of the post here and still, I can not figure out how to feed a reference genome different than hg18 (I read something about retrieving it from Ensembl, but that is not an option for me). I ran the script like this:

"myobj<-read(file.list, sample.id=list("TJ06","TJ33","TJ28","TJ29"), assembly="XXX", treatment=c(1,1,0,0),context="CG")"

and didn’t complain at all!

The same will apply to my annotation file so I will very much appreciate some guidance here.

Also, regarding the tiling windows determination (tiles=tileMethylCounts(filtered.myobj,win.size = 1000, step.size = 1000)
, it will be useless to make such an analysis without a proper reference genome specified. However, the script does it (even with completely different chromosome names/number/size in the input files than the ones in the hg18 ), Is this tiles determination based on the lowest and highest coordinate (bp) for each chromosome?

IS there any bias I am not aware when using this scripts for WGBS (rather that RRBS)?

Thanking in advance for your help ;)


Fer

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Refernce Genome not in Ensembl plus tiling windows analysis
parts:
The assembly string is for your information and at some point it will be used as a safeguard when users try to use unite() on objects from different assemblies. This has been discussed before on this forum in case the help pages are not useful. 

For the tiling, we don't need to have the genome size or assembly since the tiling operation will end when there is no more coverage on a chromosome. So you are right, tiling starts when there is coverage on chromosome and ends when there is no more coverage, and the tiles in between will be discarded if there is no coverage on them.

Best,
Altuna
